intro: Rapporter une question demande deux changements de plus qu'une affirmation : l'ordre des mots redevient celui d'une phrase affirmative et l'auxiliaire do / does / did disparaît. « Where do you live? » devient « She asked me where I lived. » On rapporte aussi les demandes et les ordres avec ask / tell + quelqu'un + to.
objectifs: Rapporter une question en Wh- avec asked + mot interrogatif + sujet + verbe (sans inversion ni do).
Rapporter une question fermée (oui / non) avec if ou whether.
Appliquer le recul des temps et les changements de pronoms et de repères vus à la leçon 104.
Rapporter une demande ou un ordre avec ask / tell + personne + (not) to + verbe.

texte: On garde le mot interrogatif (what, where, when, why, how, who, which, how much…), puis on met l'ordre d'une phrase affirmative : sujet + verbe. Il n'y a plus de point d'interrogation.
L'auxiliaire do / does / did disparaît, et le verbe reprend le temps reculé : « Where do you work? » → « He asked me where I worked. » « What did you buy? » → « She asked me what I had bought. »
Les verbes introducteurs les plus courants sont ask, want to know, wonder (se demander). Ask peut être suivi de la personne (asked me) ou non (asked).

lignes: “Where do you live?”
She asked me where I lived.
“What are you doing?”
He asked me what I was doing.
“Why did you leave?”
They asked her why she had left.
“How much does it cost?”
I asked how much it cost.
“When will you arrive?”
She wanted to know when I would arrive.
“Who has taken my pen?”
He asked who had taken his pen.

texte: Pour une question à laquelle on répond par oui ou non, on utilise if ou whether (« si »), puis l'ordre affirmatif. « Are you hungry? » → « She asked me if I was hungry. »
Whether est un peu plus soutenu et s'emploie surtout quand on présente deux possibilités : « He asked whether I wanted tea or coffee. » On dit aussi « whether or not ».
exemples: “Do you speak French?” → She asked me if I spoke French.
“Have you seen my keys?” → He asked if I had seen his keys.
“Can you help me?” → She asked me whether I could help her.
“Is it raining?” → He wanted to know if it was raining.

texte: Toutes les règles de la leçon 104 s'appliquent : recul des temps après un verbe introducteur au passé, changement des pronoms et des possessifs, et des repères de temps et de lieu (tomorrow → the next day, here → there).
Si le verbe introducteur est au présent (He asks / wants to know), on ne recule pas : « The customer wants to know when the parcel will arrive. »
exemples: “Will you come to my party tomorrow?” → She asked me if I would come to her party the next day.
will → would ; my → her ; tomorrow → the next day.
“What time does this shop close?” → The tourist wants to know what time this shop closes.
Verbe introducteur au présent : pas de recul.

sections.titre: Demandes et ordres : ask / tell + to
texte: Pour rapporter une demande polie (Could you…? Please…), on utilise ask + personne + to + verbe. Pour un ordre ou une consigne (impératif), on utilise tell + personne + to + verbe.

À la forme négative, not se place avant to : « Don't be late » → « She told me not to be late. » Ce n'est pas « She told me to not be late » (possible à l'oral, mais à éviter) ni « She told me don't be late ».

lignes: “Could you open the window, please?”
She asked me to open the window.
“Sit down.”
The teacher told us to sit down.
“Please don't smoke here.”
He asked us not to smoke there.
“Don't touch that!”
My mother told me not to touch it.

exemples: My boss asked me to send the report before Friday.
The police officer told the driver not to move.

texte: La même structure (mot interrogatif + sujet + verbe) sert dans les questions indirectes polies, au présent : « Could you tell me where the station is? », « Do you know what time it starts? ». C'est l'objet de la leçon 114.
Dans les deux cas, le piège est le même : garder l'inversion de la question directe. « Can you tell me where is the station? » est faux.
exemples: Do you know where the post office is?
Pas « where is the post office ».

formule: asked (+ personne) + wh- / if / whether + sujet + verbe (temps reculé) · asked / told + personne + (not) to + verbe
prononciation: asked /ɑːskt/ (US /æskt/) : trois consonnes à la fin, s-k-t. Ne dis pas « ask » : le -ed /t/ doit s'entendre.
Une question rapportée n'a pas l'intonation d'une question : la voix descend à la fin, comme dans une affirmation. « She asked me where I LIVED ↘. »
whether /ˈweðə/ se prononce comme weather (la météo).
Dans « told me not to », l'accent tombe sur not : « She told me NOT to wait ».
erreurs: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
Pas de did ni d'inversion dans une question rapportée.
He asked me where was the station.
He asked me where the station was.
Ordre affirmatif : sujet + verbe.
She asked me do I like coffee.
She asked me if I liked coffee.
Question fermée : if / whether.
He asked me what time is it.
He asked me what time it was.
Ordre affirmatif et recul des temps.
She asked if I was hungry?
She asked if I was hungry.
Pas de point d'interrogation.
He told me don't call him.
He told me not to call him.
Ordre négatif : told + personne + not to.
She said me to wait.
She told me to wait. / She asked me to wait.
Say ne s'emploie pas pour rapporter un ordre avec to : tell ou ask.

dialogue.contexte: Bruxelles, au retour d'un entretien d'embauche. Olivier raconte à son colocataire Emmanuel, venu de Kinshasa, les questions qu'on lui a posées.
lignes: Emmanuel
So, what did they ask you?
Alors, qu'est-ce qu'ils t'ont demandé ?
Olivier
First, they asked me why I wanted to work for them.
D'abord, ils m'ont demandé pourquoi je voulais travailler pour eux.
Emmanuel
Classic. What else?
Classique. Quoi d'autre ?
Olivier
The manager asked me if I had ever managed a team, and how many people I had worked with.
Le directeur m'a demandé si j'avais déjà géré une équipe, et avec combien de personnes j'avais travaillé.
Emmanuel
Did they ask whether you spoke Dutch?
Ils t'ont demandé si tu parlais néerlandais ?
Olivier
Yes! And they wanted to know when I could start.
Oui ! Et ils voulaient savoir quand je pourrais commencer.
Emmanuel
That sounds positive. Anything else?
Ça a l'air positif. Autre chose ?
Olivier
At the end, they asked me to send them two references and told me not to worry about the test.
À la fin, ils m'ont demandé de leur envoyer deux références et m'ont dit de ne pas m'inquiéter pour le test.

mots: She asked me where I lived.
He wanted to know how much it cost.
They asked whether I was free on Monday.
A customer enquired whether the shop was open.
The officer ordered them to stop.
She reminded me to buy bread.
rappeler (à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose)
They asked me to send two references.

exercices.consigne: Choisis la question rapportée correcte (a ou b).
items: “Where are you going?” a) She asked me where was I going. b) She asked me where I was going.
b
“Do you like jazz?” a) He asked if I liked jazz. b) He asked did I like jazz.
a
“What time is it?” a) I asked what time it was. b) I asked what time was it.
a
“Don't shout!” a) She told us to not shouting. b) She told us not to shout.
b

exercices.consigne: Rapporte la question en commençant par « She asked me… ».
items: “Where do you work?”
She asked me where I worked.
“What are you reading?”
She asked me what I was reading.
“Why did you call?”
She asked me why I had called.
“How long will you stay?”
She asked me how long I would stay.
“Who is your teacher?”
She asked me who my teacher was.

exercices.consigne: Rapporte la question avec if ou whether, en commençant par « He asked (me)… ».
items: “Are you married?”
He asked me if (whether) I was married.
“Can you drive?”
He asked me if (whether) I could drive.
“Have you finished the report?”
He asked me if (whether) I had finished the report.
“Do you want tea or coffee?”
He asked me whether I wanted tea or coffee.

exercices.consigne: Rapporte avec asked / told + personne + (not) to.
items: The doctor to me: “Stay in bed.”
The doctor told me to stay in bed.
My friend to me: “Could you lend me your car?”
My friend asked me to lend him (her) my car.
The guide to the tourists: “Don't take photos.”
The guide told the tourists not to take photos.
My neighbour to us: “Please don't make noise after ten.”
My neighbour asked us not to make noise after ten.

exercices.consigne: Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Corrige-la.
items: She asked me where did I buy my shoes.
She asked me where I had bought my shoes. / She asked me where I bought my shoes.
They asked us were we tired.
They asked us if (whether) we were tired.
He told me don't be late.
He told me not to be late.
I asked her how old is she.
I asked her how old she was.

exercices.consigne: Pense à un entretien, un rendez-vous chez le médecin ou une première rencontre. Rapporte en 4 à 5 phrases les questions qu'on t'a posées et une demande ou un ordre.
items: Exemple de réponse

Last week I went to the doctor's. She asked me how long I had had the cough. She wanted to know if I smoked and whether I was taking any medicine. Then she asked me to breathe deeply. At the end, she told me to drink a lot of water and not to go to work for two days.

a_retenir: Question en Wh- rapportée : asked + mot interrogatif + sujet + verbe (sans do, sans inversion).
Question fermée : asked + if / whether + sujet + verbe.
Recul des temps et changements de pronoms comme pour les affirmations.
Pas de point d'interrogation ni d'intonation montante.
Demande : asked + personne + to ; ordre : told + personne + to ; négation : not to.
